definition: Automated Lip Reading (ALR) is a software technology developed by speech recognition expert Frank Hubner.
details: A video image of a person talking can be analysed by the software. The shapes made by the lips can be examined and then turned into sounds. The sounds are compared to a dictionary to create matches to the words being spoken. The technology was used successfully to analyse silent home movie footage of Adolf Hitler taken by Eva Braun at their Bavarian retreat Berghof. The video, with words, was included in a documentary titled "Hitler's Private World", Revealed Studios, 2006 Source: New Technology catches Hitler off guard

explainer.lead: Automated Lip Reading (ALR) is software that turns the lip movements in video into candidate sounds and then matches them to words. Developed by speech recognition expert Frank Hubner, it offers a way to recover speech from silent footage, making it especially intriguing for historical film.

tiers.eli5: Imagine watching a friend mouth words without making any noise and guessing what they said from the shapes of their lips. ALR tries to make that guess with a computer, then checks the sounds against a dictionary to find matching words.
tiers.practitioner: Treat ALR as a video-to-word pipeline: analyse footage of a talking person, extract lip shapes, convert them into sounds, and compare those sounds with a dictionary. Its documented application is the interpretation of silent archival footage. A key pitfall is treating a dictionary match as certain when the visible movements or candidate sounds are ambiguous.
tiers.paperLevel: ALR can be expressed as video of a talking person -> lip-shape analysis -> candidate sounds -> dictionary matching -> recovered words. The technology is attributed to speech recognition expert Frank Hubner; no formal model, training procedure, or accuracy measure is specified.

explainer.example: ALR analysed silent home-movie footage of Adolf Hitler taken by Eva Braun at the Berghof. The resulting video, accompanied by the recovered words, appeared in Revealed Studios' 2006 documentary "Hitler's Private World".

usedIn.name: Hitler's Private World
usedIn.detail: The 2006 Revealed Studios documentary included silent home-movie footage of Adolf Hitler with words recovered using ALR.

usedIn.name: Silent home-movie analysis
usedIn.detail: ALR was used successfully on footage filmed by Eva Braun at the Berghof, Hitler's Bavarian retreat.

explainer.intuition: Speech leaves visible clues in the shapes and movements of the lips. ALR interprets those clues as sounds and uses a dictionary to turn them into plausible words.
howItWorks: Take a video image of a person talking.
Analyse the shapes made by the person's lips.
Turn the observed lip shapes into sounds.
Compare the sounds with a dictionary.
Select dictionary matches for the words being spoken.
explainer.whyItMatters: ALR can add a possible spoken-word interpretation to film that has no soundtrack. Its use on Hitler's home movies shows how this can give viewers a new way to engage with historical footage.
misconceptions: ALR does not recover an original audio recording; it infers sounds and words from visible lip movements.
A dictionary match is not the same as certain proof of exactly what was said.
Success on one silent film does not mean every silent video can be read equally well.
